title: Strict semilinear point transport and descent to whole derived systems
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Set $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and on the small pro-etale site set $B_n=(A_n)_s$ and $\widehat R_s=\lim_nB_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_s$ be the abelian category of strict $B_n$-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, with its ordinary unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $U_s$ for levelwise restriction to $\widehat R_s$-module towers and $\mathcal L_s=R\lim U_s$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Put $F_r=(h^r)^{-1}$ on module complexes with scalars transported through the canonical coefficient isomorphisms, and $G_r$ for its levelwise functor on systems [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Read the finite levels through $j_{r,M}:F_rM\to(h^r)^*M$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, of part (a) of the latter definition. Let $\Gamma_\bullet$ be restriction of scalars followed by exact sections levelwise, retaining all transitions [def-trf-coefficient-tower-operations, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

For $r\geq1$ and every complex $M$ of strict systems there is a unique natural $R$-linear chain map of strict towers
$$u_{r,M}:\Gamma_\bullet M\longrightarrow\Gamma_\bullet G_rM$$
whose $n$th component in the inverse-image model is $\sigma_{r,M_n}$; after the identification $\Gamma(s,j_{r,M_n})$ with the module-pullback model it is $\Gamma(s,j_{r,M_n})\sigma_{r,M_n}$, where $\sigma$ is restriction along $h^r$ followed by inverse-image colimit insertion and sheafification in the recipe [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. In the site-reindexing model $(F_rM_n)(V\xrightarrow v s)=M_n(V\xrightarrow{h^r v}s)$ the insertion identifies this $\sigma$ with the actual restriction at the final object. It is $A_n$-linear for the specified coefficient action; $j_{r,M_n}$ is an isomorphism with inverse $x\otimes a\mapsto c_n^{-1}(a)x$, where $c_n:F_rB_n\cong B_n$ is the coefficient isomorphism. For a transition $v_n:M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}M_n$, writing $\rho_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ for coefficient reduction, the tensor-insertion square has formula $x\otimes1\mapsto v_n(x)\otimes\rho_n(1)=v_n(x)\otimes1$, with completed scalar compatibility $\pi_nc_{\widehat R}=c_nF_r(\pi_n)$. These components commute with differentials and the original transitions. For every chain map $f:M\to M'$ one has
$$\Gamma_\bullet(G_rf)u_{r,M}=u_{r,M'}\Gamma_\bullet(f).$$
The two exact complex functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and this specified transformation descends to
$$I_{r,C}:\Gamma_\bullet C\longrightarrow\Gamma_\bullet G_rC,\qquad C\in D(\mathscr S_s).$$
For every morphism $f:C\to C'$ in this derived SYSTEM category,
$$\Gamma_\bullet(G_rf)I_{r,C}=I_{r,C'}\Gamma_\bullet(f).$$
When $C_n$ is bounded constructible, its $n$th evaluation, through $j_r$, is exactly $\iota^{(r)}_{C_n}$ of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. No cartesianness, boundedness or Tor-amplitude condition on the system is required.

Here the target of the descended maps is the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}R))$ of whole $R$-module towers [def-trf-coefficient-tower-operations, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The indexing $n\geq1$ is identified with the $\mathbb N$ indexing there by $n=i+1$.

proof.text: The finite construction described in this step is compiled in [lem-trf-point-system-transport-finite] with the same names, data and statements. The existing chain-level construction is now compiled in [lem-trf-point-system-transport-chain], with its original declaration names and definitions and no change in normalization. Apply [lem-trf-point-restriction-system-chain-map] with g=h^r. Its continuity and uniquely prescribed coefficient map are definitionally the ones used here, so its uniquely normalized chain map supplies chainTransport_existsUnique. Its finite coefficient naturality and the defining completed limit lift give coefficient_squares. For the finite tensor-unit comparison apply [lem-weil-finite-comparison-complex-isomorphism]; linearity of its inverse and the inverse identities give finiteComparison_inverse. For finite sigma, apply the ordinary uniquely normalized natural transformation of [lem-trf-point-restriction-section-transformation], whose construction uses scalar normalization and module-restriction naturality from [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural]. Mapping this transformation to complexes and using component extensionality gives finiteSigma_existsUnique, without a characteristic hypothesis. The named ordinary API avoids repeatedly expanding its linearity construction in this module. The tensor-transition clause is the specialization of the fully proved arbitrary-automorphism result [lem-trf-point-system-tensor-transition], constructed by conjugating the actual completed-linear transition by the normalized finite tensor comparison. This avoids the system-wide tensor-sheafification comparison and its characteristic hypothesis.

source.place: Clause (3), point-factor prerequisite to whole-system transport

proof.text: The system category is abelian with componentwise exactness by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For pull_exact, form the product of the pro-etale postcomposition equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] with the identity on the index category. The resulting equivalence on underlying abelian sheaves preserves finite limits and colimits; the faithful module forgetful functor reflects them. This proves exactness without imposing invertibility of l on the scheme. For sections_exact and finiteRSections_exact, use the independent-universe exact point-section proof from [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural], which implements [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Scalar restriction and whiskering of towers preserve finite limits and colimits. Mathlib HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_map_of_preservesHomology now proves quasi-isomorphism preservation for both termwise functors, implementing [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].

Implement [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] directly by Mathlib Localization.liftNatTrans on the localization Q of whole system complexes and whiskerRight chainTransport Q. The mapDerivedCategoryFactors isomorphisms provide its two liftings. Localization.liftNatTrans_app and the inverse identities prove the prescribed representative equation. The resulting natural transformation supplies naturality for every derived system morphism. Localization.natTrans_ext, followed by cancellation of the target factorization isomorphism, proves uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; natural-transformation form as stated in the cited DAG lemma

proof.text: Use the finite representative recipe and comparisons of [lem-trf-point-system-transport-finite]. Evaluate chainTransport at n. The identity-on-sections normalizations of the two ordinary comparisons from [lem-trf-point-system-ordinary-evaluation-comparisons] and the prescribed restriction components from [lem-trf-point-restriction-system-chain-map] identify this chain map with finiteSigmaR, using the vertical restriction identity of [lem-trf-point-restriction-sequence-evaluation]. Prove naturality of finiteSigmaR directly by module-restriction naturality, then descend its natural transformation by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Apply the general compatibility theorem [lem-trf-exact-derived-square-descent]: for a square of exact functors, the composition and natural-isomorphism factorization equations of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] show that conjugating a descended transformation by the derived square comparisons is its evaluated descent: use Localization.natTrans_ext on whole system complexes, cancel the factorization isomorphisms, apply naturality, and use the chain-level square. This identifies the evaluated derivedTransport with the descended finite sigma on every ambient derived object. Naturality transports that finite sigma to the localization's chosen representative. In the product of this representative formula with finiteDerivedComparison, the intermediate representative isomorphisms and factorization isomorphisms cancel. Functoriality of Q then combines sigma with the sheafified tensor-unit comparison into finiteTransportComplex, hence gives finiteTransportDerived. This is precisely the recipe of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] with h^r, using the finite comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. The argument retains arbitrary unbounded systems and their original transitions; it uses no faithfulness of derived evaluation, cartesianness, flatness or constructibility.

The finite construction is likewise compiled independently from chain construction and final derived descent; all original definitions and interfaces are preserved.
